messages:
dylan-docs: FYI I walked through the sample-app quickstart and hit a couple of snippet/drift problems that trip new users. The repo's .env.example uses REDWOOD_TOKEN while the SDKs/docs use REDWOOD_API_KEY. Also the Dockerfile pins node:14 but the README Node example assumes global fetch (Node 18+). Finally, the k8s/secret.yaml example sets REDWOOD_API_KEY but the deployment manifest expects REDWOOD_TOKEN — oops.

priya-sdks: ugh. which path is this?

dylan-docs: sample-app/.env.example, sample-app/docker/Dockerfile, and sample-app/k8s/{secret.yaml,deployment.yaml}. New devs copy the env file into their app and then get 401s.

ashley-devex: thanks for catching. Proposed rules: canonicalize to REDWOOD_API_KEY everywhere, update Dockerfile to node:18-alpine (or change README to use node-fetch), and add a short callout in the README: "If you run Node <18, use the CommonJS snippet (requires node-fetch@2)." That should stop a lot of the copy/paste pain.

frank-support: we had 3 tickets this month where customers pasted the sample-app env and got unauthorized. If we fix the sample app, it should cut support noise.

priya-sdks: agree. also the k8s example is inconsistent as Dylan said — secret.yaml uses REDWOOD_API_KEY but deployment.yaml envFrom uses REDWOOD_TOKEN. I'll paste a suggested k8s fix here.

dylan-docs: thanks — here's the Node snippet I'd like to put into sample-app/README.md (Docker-compatible commonjs):

```js
// Node (CommonJS) - compatible with the Docker image we build
const fetch = require('node-fetch'); // npm install node-fetch@2
const API_KEY = process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY;

fetch('https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate', {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: {
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${API_KEY}`
  },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'Hello from sample app' }),
  timeout: 10000
})
  .then(r => r.json())
  .then(console.log)
  .catch(err => console.error('Request failed', err));
```

priya-sdks: and here's the k8s snippet to keep names aligned (secret + deployment):

```yaml
# k8s/secret.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: redwood-secret
type: Opaque
stringData:
  REDWOOD_API_KEY: "{{ .Values.redwoodApiKey }}"
---
# k8s/deployment.yaml (partial)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: sample-app
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: sample-app:latest
          envFrom:
            - secretRef:
                name: redwood-secret
```

ashley-devex: perfect. Two small extras: 1) add a one-liner near the top of the README: "SDKs include exponential backoff by default; the sample-app HTTP examples are one-shot unless you use the SDK." 2) add a note in the Docker section about Node version and that the image will install node-fetch@2 if using node:14.

frank-support: can we also add a tiny CI check in the repo that validates env var names in the README vs .env.example? A quick grep test would cut regressions.

priya-sdks: good idea — I'll add a GitHub Actions job that runs a script to check for REDWOOD_API_KEY vs any legacy names. If mismatch, fail CI and print the offending files.

dylan-docs: opened PR with fixes and the CI check: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-app/pull/206 — changes: canonicalize env var to REDWOOD_API_KEY, update Dockerfile to node:18-alpine, add CommonJS Node snippet + Node18 ESM variant, align k8s manifests, and add docs note about retry behavior.

ops-bot: docs site rebuild queued (job 12234). ETA ~ 6m.

ashley-devex: once this merges I'll add the sample-app link to the onboarding checklist and ping SEs to use the updated repo during first-run tests. Also filing a tiny docs-ui follow-up to add copy buttons on the sample-app README code blocks.

priya-sdks: i'll also bump the sample-app tag in the SDK quickstart mapping so internal runbooks refer to the fixed version.

frank-support: thanks y'all — will keep an eye on support tickets after the deploy. closing after the PR merges. :thumbsup:
